And the opening works so effectively because it corrupted audience expectations by flipping the lens. While the world was waiting to see Jack, Sawyer and Kate, we were introduced to a suburban book club that didn't belong. This wasn't just a clever reveal; it was a total expansion of the show's universe.

 It forces the audience to view the crash of flight Oceanic 815 literally tear in half in the sky through the eyes of the Others which instantly transformed the Others from shadowy myths into calculated observers, proving the Island was never empty and that they were never truly safe.
